campus_notes: NYU Residential Life publishes no room dimensions or square footage for its residence halls. Per-floor floor plans exist for every hall (PNG, linked per dorm via housing.nyu.edu) but NYU states they are not drawn to scale. Room inventory and rates are the official proposed 2026-27 table (https://www.nyu.edu/students/student-information-and-resources/housing-and-dining/on-campus-living/application-and-assignments/rates-and-payments.html); rates are per person per semester. Halls are scattered across Manhattan (Greenwich Village/Union Square area) and Downtown Brooklyn rather than a contiguous campus. Furnishings per resident (official what-to-bring guide): bed, twin mattress, desk, desk chair, drawer space, and closet/wardrobe space; beds are Twin XL (80") except Clark Street's standard twin (75"); personal furniture may not be added; all windows have blinds. Student AC units are only permitted in apartment-suite kitchens (halls otherwise have building AC where listed). 'In Unit' room types are bedrooms inside shared suites/apartments; 'Studio' types are self-contained rooms. NYU Law runs its own separate halls (D'Agostino, Hayden) with published approximate dimensions; they are law-school housing and not part of this Residential Life inventory.

dorms.notes: Situated in the heart of the East Village, Alumni Hall is home to approximately 450 upper-year students. Most residents enjoy private single bedrooms within shared suites, alongside several ADA accessible double rooms. Each suite accommodates 2-4 residents and comes furnished with a bed, desk, closet, and dresser per bedroom, plus a common area featuring a refrigerator, stove, sink, and cabinets. Single bedroom suites also include a table and chairs. The building offers two main lounges, a TV lounge with a pool table and a spacious study lounge, as well as smaller study lounges on floors 2-6 and 13-15. Laundry facilities are located in the basement.

dorms.notes: Broome Street is uniquely situated between New York City’s historic Little Italy and the vibrant, trend-setting SoHo neighborhood. This residence hall serves as a supportive living-learning community for about 350 upper-year students, including sophomores, juniors, and seniors. The community offers a strong residential support network, including a Faculty Fellow in Residence, two Faculty Affiliates, a student-led BEAST Hall Council, and a dedicated team of eight undergraduate Resident Assistants. Together, they provide programming that fosters community involvement and encourages residents to explore the city.

dorms.notes: Welcome to Founders Hall, home to over 700 first-year students, located in the Union Square/East Village area of NYC! Built on the site of the former St. Ann’s church, the historic façade and fence have been preserved as part of the front courtyard. To help facilitate the community, enhance your academic experience, plan events, and provide support, there are 25 Resident Assistants, one Resource Center Assistant, three student affairs professionals and two Faculty Fellows-in-Residence. With 26 floors, Founders features a large outdoor courtyard, two TV lounges, one study lounge with computers, wi-fi access throughout the lobby and lounges, recycling/trash rooms on every floor, a laundry room, and energy and sustainability-focused features. dorms.notes: Located in Downtown Brooklyn, the Donald F. and Mildred Topp Othmer Residence Hall is an 18-story building, housing over 400 NYU students in both traditional and apartment-style suites. The residence includes a large outdoor courtyard, student lounge access on each floor, and laundry facilities in the basement. Our 12 Resident Assistants (RAs) and one Faculty Fellow-in-Residence are here to help facilitate community building, enhance your academic experience, plan events, and provide support during your time at Othmer Hall. dorms.notes: Nestled in the heart of the East Village, Seventh Street is a vibrant residence hall on the south side of 7th Street between 2nd and 3rd Avenues. Home to roughly 90 upper-year students, this close-knit community shares programming and staff with its neighboring hall, Sixth Street. Apartments here are primarily quads, four residents sharing some of the most spacious living arrangements on campus. Each unit features generous closet space, room to study comfortably, and common areas equipped with a refrigerator, sink, cabinets, a couch, and dining furniture. Beyond your apartment, Seventh Street offers a range of freshly renovated amenities: a TV lounge with a full kitchen, a dedicated study lounge, and a game room with table tennis and foosball. Additional perks include first-floor bike storage, a lending library, and basement laundry.
